name: Parquet Courts
label: Rough Trade
lede: Four Texans in Brooklyn put their second album out as 500 records cut during sick days, refused to stay in frame for photo shoots, and a decade later were cutting 40-minute jams in the Catskills for Rough Trade.

hero.by: Thalia Hall, Chicago, February 2016. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Knights of the Round Turntable
eras.text: Andrew Savage grew up in Denton, Texas, trading tapes through Maximumrocknroll and starting a college club where people sat through whole LPs. He went to New York first and talked the others into following.

years.h: Three Denton friends and a kid brother start Parquet Courts in Brooklyn
years.p: Andrew Savage and [[Austin Brown|50dec28e-63a9-4d97-864d-aa9923ade531]] met at the University of North Texas. With bassist Sean Yeaton and Savage's younger brother Max on drums, they form the band in New York.
years.xp:
Savage started a club at college called Knights of the Round Turntable, where members gathered to listen to one vinyl album all the way through. Brown was a member. Savage had already played in Denton bands including Teenage Cool Kids and Fergus & Geronimo.

In New York, he told the Guardian, he got by dealing dope from the back of his bike: "It's not something I'm doing now but it's something I might probably do again in the future, so I don't really want to talk about it."

Looking back in 2023, he noted that three of them were 24 when they started and Max was 18.

years.h: American Specialties comes out on cassette only
years.p: The debut is a limited tape on Play Pinball!. Rough Trade finally reissues it ten years later.
years.xp: "Cassettes force you to be patient and digest what you're listening to," Savage told the Guardian. "I like to reward people's curiosity."

eras.title: Snotty young Lou Reeds
eras.text: Light Up Gold won them acclaim on both sides of the Atlantic, and they made the press work for it. Two more records came out inside two years, one of them by only half the band under a different name.

years.src: The Guardian (2013) · Wikipedia: Light Up Gold
years.h: Light Up Gold, cut in three days on sick days
years.p: Savage's own Dull Tools label presses 500 copies. Yeaton's office was so close to the studio that he couldn't leave until his co-workers had gone home.
years.xp: Jonathan Schenke recorded, mixed and mastered it: 15 songs in 33 minutes. NME gave it 9/10. In 2025 Rolling Stone put it on its list of the greatest albums of the century so far.

years.cap: Parquet Courts in Austin during SXSW, March 2013
years.src: Wikipedia: Light Up Gold · Wikipedia: Parquet Courts
years.h: What's Your Rupture? reissues Light Up Gold nationwide
years.p: The Brooklyn label takes it beyond the first 500, and it reaches No. 25 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.

q: Warming is not the word I'd use. We've thawed to it.
years.h: An English pub with a thatched roof tests Savage's manners
years.p: After a year of curt interviews and photo shoots where they wouldn't stay in shot, the band try to say nice things about Britain. Savage manages that the thatched roof was "charming."
years.xp:
Brown liked "the regimen of the English breakfast." Savage liked walking around with a beer in his hand.

The same month they put out the EP Tally All the Things That You Broke. Savage said he was going off video interviews: "It's the unease that you get when you feel like you're a commodity."

years.src: Wikipedia: Sunbathing Animal · Wikipedia: Parquet Courts
years.h: Sunbathing Animal puts them in the UK top 60
years.p: Their third album, recorded in three sessions in Brooklyn and the Catskills, comes out on What's Your Rupture? with Rough Trade in the UK. It reaches No. 55 there.
years.xp: Brown said the lyrics came first and were "meant to be right at the front." Pitchfork gave it 8.6 and later ranked it No. 140 of the 2010s.

years.src: Wikipedia: Content Nausea · Wikipedia: Parquet Courts
years.h: Half the band makes Content Nausea as Parkay Quarts
years.p: With Yeaton and Max Savage busy, Andrew Savage and Brown record it themselves on a four-track cassette in under two weeks.
years.xp: The Parkay Quarts name had appeared a month earlier on the single 'Uncast Shadow of a Southern Myth'. Pitchfork's Mike Powell found it easier to listen to than Sunbathing Animal.

eras.title: Living in the studio
eras.text: The band joined Rough Trade properly, tried free improvisation, and then moved into an upstate studio to make Human Performance. Savage painted its cover and got a Grammy nomination for it.

years.h: Wilco's Solid Sound festival books them in North Adams
years.p: The same year they make Ramsgate with PC Worship as PCPC and release Live at Third Man Records.

years.h: Monastic Living is pure improvisation, and Pitchfork hates it
years.p: The mostly instrumental Rough Trade EP is, the band said, their first time improvising outright. Pitchfork gives it 4.9; Spin gives it 7.

years.src: Wikipedia: Human Performance · Wikipedia: Parquet Courts
years.h: Human Performance, made while living at Dreamland
years.p: Recorded largely while the band lived at Dreamland Recording Studios in Hurley, New York. Savage's own painting on the cover earns a Grammy nomination for Best Recording Package.
years.xp:
"We were living there, working around the clock, and there was never any time where we couldn't be loud," Savage said. He compared it to the White Album, except "the whole band was getting along and nobody's girlfriend was there."

It reached No. 50 in the UK, and Rolling Stone put it at No. 9 on its albums of 2016.

years.h: A solo Savage album, and a record with Karen O
years.p: Savage releases Thawing Dawn as A. Savage on Dull Tools. Two weeks later comes Milano, the band's album with Italian composer Daniele Luppi, with [[Karen O|14d44067-99c2-4f77-b58b-138f0b6911fa]] of the [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs|584c04d2-4acc-491b-8a0a-e63133f4bfc4]] singing.

eras.title: Punk, funk and a dub station
eras.text: A pop producer with polished records to his name took them to a ranch on the Texas border, and the band came back dancing. The next album went further, into techno and club culture, before the band stopped touring.

q: I liked that it didn't make sense.
Andrew Savage, on hiring Danger Mouse
years.src: Wikipedia: Wide Awake! · Wikipedia: Parquet Courts
yt: 'Almost Had to Start a Fight/In and Out of Patience'
years.h: Wide Awake!: Danger Mouse on a punk-funk record
years.p: Recorded at Sonic Ranch in Tornillo, Texas, and Electric Lady in New York, December 2017 to January 2018. Australia's Double J names it album of the year.
years.xp:
Savage: "I was writing a record that indebted to punk and funk, and Brian's a pop producer who's made some very polished records." He called the opening track "a bit like a manifesto" about collectivity and individuality.

It reached No. 27 in the UK. Paste ranked it the second-best album of 2018.

years.src: Wikipedia: Parquet Courts · Wikipedia: Wide Awake!
years.p: The Wide Awake! opener goes to No. 2 on the UK physical singles chart. The band spend 2018 and 2019 touring the album.

years.h: Rough Trade announces the American Specialties reissue
years.p: The cassette-only debut gets its first wide release, a decade on.

years.cap: Parquet Courts at Rockwood Music Hall, New York
years.src: Wikipedia: Sympathy for Life · Wikipedia: Parquet Courts
years.p: Producers Rodaidh McDonald and [[John Parish|4ae92e70-3690-473b-8fbc-49749565669f]] help shape Catskills jams that ran up to 40 minutes. Brown runs a 16-channel dub station.
years.xp:
After the long Wide Awake! tour, Brown and Savage had been listening to dance and techno. "I didn't really feel like making another rock record," Brown said. Savage called him "the control master of the jam."

The lead single, 'Plant Life', came with a ten-minute extended cut. The album reached No. 42 in the UK and No. 14 in Scotland.

years.cap: Parquet Courts at the Queen Elizabeth Theatre, Toronto, March 2022
years.h: Mdou Moctar opens their North American tour
years.p: The Nigerien guitarist supports on dates through March.

years.cap: Parquet Courts at Oya festival, Oslo, August 2022
years.h: Green Man in Wales is the last show to date
years.p: They play the festival in Crickhowell, a few months after their North American tour. No show has followed.

eras.title: Hiatus, not a breakup
eras.text: Andrew Savage went back to his solo records. The others had families and their own projects, and the band said it hadn't ended.

q: We will definitely do something again. Rest assured.
years.h: Savage's Several Songs About Fire, and a promise
years.p: Asked about the band, Savage told Post Trash they were on hiatus, not broken up.
years.xp: "When we started three of us were 24, and Max was 18. Our twenties were spent touring," he said. "I'm 37 now, and I'm probably the one that's most eager to tour. The other guys have wives and children."

sources.title: The Guardian (2013): Parquet Courts: 'We've thawed towards the UK'
